beats.narration_text: Rhodes Daily is a single-player extraction action RPG. You take operators down one-way floors, and on every floor you decide: push deeper, or get out. What you bring out feeds a base you run and trade from. Done, it will be a Windows build plus a test suite anyone can rerun from a fresh clone. Godot four point seven, Forward plus on Direct3D twelve.

beats.narration_text: Why care? The extraction choice comes back every floor while danger grows with depth, and the loot feeds a base economy that runs on scaled real time.
beats.new_visual_element: Danger curve rising per floor; arrow into base economy

production_viz.label: Push or extract
production_viz.mechanic: Floors as a descending stack, danger line rising, an extract arrow at every floor, all arrows feeding one base box.

beats.narration_text: Two games I played. In Escape from Duckov a raid is one map; here a run is a stack of floors, so the choice returns every floor. Greedy Cave gave me the one-way descent; this adds telegraphed real-time combat and a nine-faction economy. Whether that is more fun, playtests will decide.

production_viz.label: Compared with
production_viz.mechanic: Two text-only cards (no logos, no footage of other games): Duckov one map vs. stacked floors; Greedy Cave descent vs. telegraphed combat + nine-faction economy.

beats.narration_text: Who opens it? A hiring manager or lead, hiring a gameplay programmer or technical designer. Double-click: title, new save, tutorial, base, first run. A new save walks a short story first; I have not timed it against sixty seconds yet, and I will.

beats.narration_text: What it proves. Shaders: the fire's predicted pixels matched measurement at thirty, sixty and a hundred forty-four frames a second. Particles and animation: assignments six and seven. Profiling: switching to Direct3D twelve took the mine from about nine to about a hundred fifty frames a second on an RTX 4060 laptop; measured once, and I will commit the log. Verification: a headless suite with fixed seeds, a simulation that plays the main story, human checks, and Claude Code directed through written briefs.
beats.corner_tag: Constructed · evidence from A5 TEST-REPORT and repo

production_viz.label: Skill → evidence
production_viz.mechanic: Five rows: shaders (A5 pixel table excerpt), particles (a6), animation (a7), profiling (9→150 fps, marked 'log to be committed'), verification (run_all output excerpt).

beats.narration_text: What is left: music, optimising how the systems work together, and bug testing. Out of scope: multiplayer.

production_viz.label: Done · Will · Out
production_viz.mechanic: Three columns. Done: loop, regions, base, A5–A7. Will: music, cross-system optimisation, bug testing. Out: multiplayer.

beats.narration_text: The risk: the game is big and its systems interlock; change one number and another drifts. The flow simulation already shows money as a bottleneck, and a first voyage near one point oh eight million, simulated, not playtested. So every change gets the economy probe and the flow simulation, a balance log, and human playtests.
beats.new_visual_element: Linked system nodes, one change ripples

production_viz.label: Interlocking systems
production_viz.mechanic: Nodes: economy, exchange, research, contracts, time scale, voyage. Nudge one, edges light up in sequence.

beats.narration_text: Why this project? A mix. Systems and numbers design I already had; the repo's design documents and simulations show it. Shaders, particles, Blender, animation and Godot itself were new this course, each a tagged assignment.

production_viz.label: Had · New
production_viz.mechanic: Two columns. Had: systems/numbers design → repo docs, probe, test_flow. New: a3 Blender, a5 shaders, a6 particles, a7 animation.
